text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.
CORN SALE - Taiwan's Members Feed Industry Group bought a shipment of 56,000 to 60,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 corn from Tradi Grain at a tender on Friday, traders said.
WHEAT SALES - South Korea's Cheiljedang Corp and Dongah Flour Mills Co Ltd jointly bought 34,000 tonnes of U.S. No.1 wheat from Japanese trading house Nichimen Corp, traders said.
- Iraq bought 50,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat at $187 per tonne, including freight for delivery to Umm Qasr.

WHEAT SALES - The CCC bought 6,500 tonnes of U.S. No. 2 or better hard red winter wheat for donation to Armenia and 6,500 tonnes of U.S. HRW wheat for donation to Georgia. The two 6,500-tonne shipments were bought from Continental Grain at $148.17, FOB, Beaumont, Texas, the CCC said.

Armenia also bought 1,134 tonnes of U.S. No. 2 or better HRW wheat in bulk under the PL-480, Title I export program, its U.S. export agent said. That wheat was 12 percent protein at $148.49 a tonne, FOB, Beaumont, the agent said.
The delivery dates for all shipments were August 20 to September 8.

DURUM SALE - Syria's General Establishment for Cereal Processing and Trade (GECPT) last month sold Algeria 150,000 tonnes of hard amber durum wheat for September/August delivery, a GECPT official told Reuters on Wednesday.
He did not reveal the price but said the deal was sealed in late July after a tender issued by Algeria.
WHEAT TENDERS - The CCC said it was seeking on August 12, upto 30,000 tonnes of U.S. No. 2 or better soft white wheat for donation to Pakistan. Shipment period was slated for August 24-September 18.

WHEAT TENDERS - Morocco, which earlier postponed a tender for up to 130,000 tonnes of soft wheat, re-entered the grain market with a tender to import 90,000 tonnes, European grain traders said. Results of the tender are due on August 12.
- The CCC will tender on August 11 for 27,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat for donation to Eritrea. The shipment is August 24-September 13.
- Jordan is tendering on August 12 for 100,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat. One shipment of 50,000 tonnes is for October delivery and the rest for November, European traders said.
BARLEY TENDER - European grain traders said on Tuesday Morocco was tendering for 30,000 tonnes of feed barley to be delivered between August 22 and 31.

WHEAT/CORN TENDER - The Cyprus Grain Commission issued tenders for a combined shipment of 14,000 of spring wheat and 8,000 tonnes of durum wheat for September shipment. It was also seeking 18,000 tonnes of corn due for September shipment.

RICE TENDER - Syria's General Foreign Trade Organisation for Chemicals and Foodstuffs issued a tender to buy 12,000 tonnes of white rice for August delivery. September 1 was set as final date to receive bids. Results would be on Sept 8.

VEGOIL TENDERS - El Salvador was seeking approximately 4,000 to 5,000 tonnes prime bleachable summer yellow (PBSY) cottonseed oil in bulk and about 750 to 1,240 tonnes sunflowerseed oil under the PL-480, Title 1 export program, its U.S. export agent said. Both commodities were slated for October 1-15 shipment. Offers were due on August 14.

- Egypt's official Holding Company for Food Industries was seeking on August 19 10,000 to 20,000 tonnes of crude sunflower and/or semi-refined cottonseed oil for delivery in the second half of September.

MARKET TALK - China will load 87,500 tonnes of corn to ship to South Korea in August and September at a CIF (cost, insurance and freight) cost of $140.20 and $143.35 a tonne, China Economic Times said on Wednesday.

Two lots totalling 49,000 tonnes were loaded for South Korea in June and August, the newspaper said, without detailing the price. Corn exported to Malaysia totalled 25,000 tonnes, loaded in April at a CIF cost of $150 a tonne, it said. China decided to export corn in a bearish domestic market in the hope that falling prices could be reversed, it said.
... European grain traders said they had been asked to supply 24,000 tonnes of European Union maize for distribution as food aid in famine-struck North Korea.
